# Seabound
Onboard carbon capture for ships

Builds carbon capture equipment that fits on ships to capture exhaust CO2 at the source. Y Combinator alumnus.

Seabound is raising a Series A round to scale-up the team, technology, and commercial deployments.

Sector: Shipping decarbonisation
Location: London, United Kingdom
Stage: seed
Founded: 2021
Website: https://www.seabound.co
Blue economy sector: shipping and ports
Development stage: demo operational env
Funding stage: seed
Legal form: limited company
Registry status: active
Team size: 23
Employees: 10-49
Total raised: 6,974,660
Raising now: 13,000,000 EUR (open)

## Readiness
KTH Innovation Readiness Level 1-9, assessed 2026-10-16, low confidence
- Customer (CRL) 6: Customer testing confirms value; structured sales activities started.
- Technology (TRL) 6: Representative prototype demonstrated in a relevant environment.
- Business model (BRL) 5: Revenue and cost sides validated with external feedback; P&L updated.
- IP (IPRL) 5: Draft IP strategy; first formal application of key IP filed.
- Team (TMRL) 6: Complementary, diverse founding team with clear CEO; advisors being recruited.
- Funding (FRL) 6: Improved pitch tested; 3-5 year P&L and cash flow.
Seed-stage hardware moving through ship pilots, with government grant support.

## Ocean impact
- Towards 1.5C, SOx emissions mitigated (D5): Co-capture of sulphur emissions (claimed). (claimed)
- Towards 1.5C, GHG emissions reduced or avoided (D1): Captures CO2 from ship exhaust onboard. (qualitative evidence)

## Funding
- seed: 4,400,000 USD (2022-05), led by Lowercarbon Capital. With Eastern Pacific Shipping, Emles, Hawktail, Rebel Fund, Soma Capital, Y Combinator.
- Grant: Reported by aggregators; verify against the UK DfT announcement. from UK Clean Maritime Demonstration Competition (Round 6), 1,100,000 GBP (2025)
- Accelerator: Y Combinator Winter 2022
